# Scrip

> Self-hosted, simulated PIX payment gateway for development and CI - in the spirit of MinIO
> (S3) or LocalStack (AWS), but for a payment gateway's lifecycle. Not a production system:
> it does not process real payments or connect to the Central Bank/SPI.

Scrip reproduces the behavior of a real PIX gateway - QR code generation, asynchronous
confirmation, expiration, refunds, signed webhooks, merchant KYC - with no external provider.
Two physically separate route surfaces share the same underlying data: `/v1/api/*` (Bearer
JWT, called by the merchant's own backend) and `/v1/panel/*` (HTTP Basic, the admin panel).
The API base URL defaults to `http://localhost:8081` in development and is whatever
`VITE_API_BASE_URL` / the deployment's origin is otherwise.

## Integration API (`/v1/api`, `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`)

- POST /v1/api/payments/pix/charges: Creates a PIX charge. Body: amount (required, integer
  cents), payer_document, payer_name, description, metadata (object), callback_url (overrides
  the store's webhook_url for this charge's events only). Accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header.
- GET /v1/api/payments/charges: Lists the store's charges, any payment method. Query: status,
  from, to (ISO 8601), limit, offset.
- GET /v1/api/payments/charges/{id}: Looks up one charge.
- GET /v1/api/payments/charges/{id}/events: Lists a charge's status transition history.
- POST /v1/api/payments/charges/{id}/cancel: Cancels a pending charge.
- POST /v1/api/payments/charges/{id}/refunds: Requests a refund. Body: amount (optional,
  defaults to the full outstanding balance), reason.
- GET /v1/api/payments/charges/{id}/refunds: Lists a charge's refunds.
- GET /v1/api/merchants/me: Looks up the authenticated store's data (webhook_secret included).
- PATCH /v1/api/merchants/me: Updates the store's name, webhook_url, rotates its
  webhook_secret, or sets its PIX fees: `pix_fee_in_bps`/`pix_fee_out_bps` (integer, 0-10000
  basis points, i.e. 0-100%) and `pix_fee_in_fixed`/`pix_fee_out_fixed` (integer cents) for
  the entry/exit fee's percentage and flat components.
- POST /v1/api/withdrawals: Requests a payout of the store's available balance. Body: amount
  (required, integer cents). The store's exit fee (`pix_fee_out_fixed +
  amount * pix_fee_out_bps`) is computed at request time and reserved together with `amount`
  against `available` immediately, before it's confirmed - `amount + fee` can't exceed
  `available` or the request is rejected with `insufficient_balance`.
- GET /v1/api/withdrawals: Lists the store's withdrawals. Query: status (pending, confirmed,
  denied), limit, offset.
- GET /v1/api/withdrawals/{id}: Looks up one withdrawal.

A charge response has `payment_method: "pix"` at the top level and PIX-only fields (qr_code,
qr_code_txid, qr_code_expires_at, e2e_id) nested under a `pix` object - future payment methods
would nest their own fields the same way instead of adding to the flat charge shape. Full shape:
`id`, `object: "charge"`, `merchant_id`, `payment_method`, `status`, `amount`,
`amount_refunded`, `payer_document`, `payer_name`, `description`, `metadata`, `callback_url`,
`fee_amount`, `pix: {...}`, `paid_at`, `expired_at`, `canceled_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at`.
`status` is one of `pending`, `paid`, `expired`, `canceled` (one L), `partially_refunded`,
`refunded`. `fee_amount` is the store's entry fee (see Concepts > Fees) - zero until the
charge is paid, then fixed for the charge's lifetime even across a later refund. A withdrawal
has the same idea on the exit side: its `fee_amount` is set once, at creation.

There is no real bank behind a withdrawal, so confirming or denying one is a panel-only
action (POST /v1/panel/withdrawals/{id}/confirm or /deny, Basic auth) - not exposed on
/v1/api. Confirming keeps the amount debited; denying releases it back to `available`.

## Concepts

- Auth: a Bearer JWT is minted from the panel (Tokens screen), and is scoped to one store -
  there is no cross-store or per-route permission model. This is scriptable, no browser
  needed: `POST /v1/panel/merchants` (no auth, body: `name` optional) creates a store and
  returns its `id`; `POST /v1/panel/tokens` (HTTP Basic, username is that `id`, password is
  ignored - any value works, including empty; body: `name` optional label, `expires_in`
  optional e.g. `"24h"`) mints the JWT. Both are on the `/v1/panel` Basic-auth surface, not
  `/v1/api`.
- Idempotency: repeating `Idempotency-Key` with the same body on charge creation replays the
  original response instead of creating a second charge; the same key with a different body
  is rejected (`409 idempotency_key_reused`).
- Webhooks: `pix.charge.created`, `pix.charge.paid`, `pix.charge.expired`,
  `pix.charge.refunded`, `kyc.approved`, `kyc.rejected`, `withdrawal.confirmed`,
  `withdrawal.denied` - signed with HMAC-SHA256 over `<timestamp>.<body>`, sent as
  `X-Scrip-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex hmac>`, alongside `X-Scrip-Event`, `X-Scrip-Delivery`
  (delivery id, stable across retries) and `X-Scrip-Attempt`. The POSTed body is
  `{ id, event, created_at, data }`, where `data` holds the affected resource(s) keyed by
  name: `{ charge }` for `pix.charge.*` (`pix.charge.refunded` adds `refund` alongside it),
  `{ withdrawal }` for `withdrawal.*`, `{ merchant, reason }` for `kyc.*`. If your webhook
  receiver runs on the host and Scrip runs in the container from the provided
  docker-compose.yml, it can't reach `localhost:<port>` on the host - add
  `extra_hosts: ["host.docker.internal:host-gateway"]` to the `app` service and point
  `webhook_url` at `http://host.docker.internal:<port>/...`.
- Errors: every failure is `{ "error": { "code", "message", "details"? } }`, with a stable
  machine-readable `code`. Codes relevant to `/v1/api`: `api_auth_required`, `token_not_found`,
  `token_revoked`, `token_expired`, `invalid_token`, `merchant_not_found`, `invalid_amount`,
  `invalid_metadata`, `kyc_required`, `charge_not_found`, `invalid_state_transition`,
  `charge_not_refundable`, `refund_exceeds_charge`, `refund_not_found`, `insufficient_balance`,
  `invalid_withdrawal_status`, `withdrawal_not_found`, `invalid_webhook_url`, `invalid_name`,
  `idempotency_key_reused`. Not an exhaustive list - `code` is a free-form string, not a
  closed enum.
- Test `payer_document`s: `11111111111` always confirms at the minimum delay, `22222222222`
  never confirms (runs to expiration), `33333333333` confirms but its webhook deliveries fail
  on purpose - useful for exercising retry handling in CI without waiting on real odds.
  Any other document confirms per `approvalRate` (85% by default).
- Simulated time: pending charges auto-confirm or expire on a delay driven by config, or can
  be forced immediately from the panel with POST /v1/panel/charges/{id}/simulate (Body:
  result, "paid" or "expired") for deterministic tests.
- KYC gate: charge creation is unrestricted by default; setting `requireApprovedKycForCharges`
  rejects it with `403 kyc_required` for any merchant whose `kyc_status` isn't `approved`.
- Fees: a store's PIX fee is "fixed + %" per direction, same shape real gateways use (e.g.
  Stripe's 2.9% + $0.30) - see the `PATCH /v1/api/merchants/me` fields above. The entry fee is
  computed off the store's rate at the moment a charge is marked `paid`; the exit fee at the
  moment a withdrawal is created. Both are snapshotted onto that charge/withdrawal's
  `fee_amount`, so a later rate change never reaches back into money that already moved - and
  a charge's fee is kept even if it's later refunded.
- Balance: `available` = settled charges - refunds - entry fees - pending/confirmed
  withdrawals (payout + exit fee). `withdrawn` (confirmed-only withdrawal total, gross of the
  exit fee) and `fees_in`/`fees_out` (entry/exit fee totals) are informational - all three are
  already reflected in `available`.

- [Full interactive documentation](/documentacao): browsable, per-route request/response
  schemas and a live playground to execute real calls against the configured API.
